Sequence integrity, stated because this log is published and the property is checkable. Two numbers in it are wrong: seq 50 appears twice, on lines 50 and 51, and seq 55 was never issued. Nothing was edited and nothing was removed. Before commit 7fc3ec6 the sequence was a counter cached when a Ledger was constructed and guarded by a threading.Lock, which protects one process against itself and says nothing to the four other processes writing this file. The assignment guard was started while the file held 49 lines. The calibration job then wrote line 50 and took seq 50. At 19:30:35 on 31 August the guard, still counting from 49, issued 50 a second time and then ran exactly one behind for five records, so lines 51 to 55 carry seq 50 to 54. The guard was restarted, recounted 55 lines, and issued 56, which is why 55 belongs to no record. Every line after 55 is correct. The sequence is now recounted inside an advisory file lock held across the append, so no two processes can agree on a number. tests/test_ledger.py holds four processes to it and fails against the implementation that produced this.

Replaced the standing fee bound with a measurement. Alpaca's own fee activities for 31 August total 6.62 dollars across 140 executed contracts, which is 0.047286 per contract. The ledger's cash reconciliation for the same day reaches the same figure independently, so two routes agree. The standing bound was 0.20 per contract, commission and regulatory pass-through at 0.10 each, deliberately set above any plausible retail fee while no fill existed to measure. The broker reports one fee bucket and does not separate the two, so the whole measured amount now sits in costs.per_contract_fee and costs.regulatory_fee_per_contract is zero because it is accounted for in the other field rather than assumed away. Both keys leave provenance.conservative_bound. The effect is small and is stated rather than implied: replaying the 1 September chain, candidates whose gross profit is entirely consumed by cost fall from 440 of 1383 to 433 of 1383. Execution cost on these structures is dominated by the half-spread, not by fees.
